questions.title: Student Record Using a Class
questions.objective: Define a class with fields, create an object, and assign and read its fields.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class named Student with public fields name (String) and marks (int). In main(), read the student's details, create one Student object using the default constructor, assign the input values to the fields, and print them.

The name contains no spaces. Assume all input is valid.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The object stores the name and marks, which are printed with the required labels.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: student name.
Line 2: marks.
questions.output_format:
Name: <name>
Marks: <marks>
questions.constraints:
Name length: 1–50 characters.
0 ≤ marks ≤ 100
hints: Declare class Student (without public) above class Main, with the fields String name; and int marks;.
Create the object with Student s = new Student(); then assign s.name and s.marks.
Print using the object's fields: "Name: " + s.name.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: student name.
Line 2: marks.
extra_fields.output_format:
Name: <name>
Marks: <marks>

questions.title: Rectangle Area and Perimeter
questions.objective: Write instance methods that compute values from an object's fields.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class named Rectangle with double fields length and width. Implement calculateArea() returning length × width and calculatePerimeter() returning 2 × (length + width).

Read the two dimensions, create a Rectangle object, assign the dimensions, and call both methods. Format both results to exactly two decimal places using Locale.US so the decimal separator is always a period.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The area is 5 × 3 = 15, and the perimeter is 2 × (5 + 3) = 16.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: length.
Line 2: width.
questions.output_format:
Area: <area to 2 decimal places>
Perimeter: <perimeter to 2 decimal places>
questions.constraints: 0.01 ≤ length, width ≤ 10,000
hints: Methods inside the class can use the fields directly: return length * width;.
Call the methods on the object: r.calculateArea().
Format with String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f", value) and import java.util.Locale.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: length.
Line 2: width.
extra_fields.output_format:
Area: <area to 2 decimal places>
Perimeter: <perimeter to 2 decimal places>

questions.title: Bank Account with Encapsulation
questions.objective: Protect a private field and change it only through validated methods.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class BankAccount with a private long field balance. Implement these public methods:
- deposit(long amount): add the amount to the balance.
- withdraw(long amount): subtract the amount only when amount is positive and amount <= balance. Otherwise, leave the balance unchanged.
- getBalance(): return the current balance.
Read the initial balance, then process all deposits in order, followed by all withdrawals in order. A withdrawal equal to the balance is valid and leaves the balance at zero.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Deposits raise the balance to 1500. Withdrawals of 100 and 800 leave 600. The final withdrawal leaves 550.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: initial balance.
Line 2: number of deposits, D.
Next D lines: deposit amounts.
Next line: number of withdrawals, W.
Next W lines: withdrawal amounts.
questions.output_format: Print the final balance as an integer.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ initial balance ≤ 10^12
0 ≤ D, W ≤ 100
Each transaction amount is between 1 and 10^9.
The balance never exceeds 10^15.
hints: Give BankAccount a constructor that takes the initial balance, since the field is private.
In withdraw, check amount > 0 && amount <= balance before subtracting.
main() can only read the balance through getBalance().

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: initial balance.
Line 2: number of deposits, D.
Next D lines: deposit amounts.
Next line: number of withdrawals, W.
Next W lines: withdrawal amounts.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the final balance as an integer.

questions.title: Constructor and Getter Methods
questions.objective: Initialize private fields with a parameterized constructor and read them with getters.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Employee with private fields id (int) and salary (double). Implement a parameterized constructor that initializes both fields, plus public methods getId() and getSalary().

Read the employee's details, construct an Employee object using the parameterized constructor, and print its values using the getter methods. Format salary to exactly two decimal places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The constructor initializes the private fields. The getters provide controlled access to their values.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: employee ID.
Line 2: monthly salary.
questions.output_format:
ID: <id>
Salary: <salary to 2 decimal places>
hints: Inside the constructor, use this.id = id; when the parameter has the same name as the field.
Create the object in one step: new Employee(id, salary).
Format the salary with String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f", e.getSalary()).

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: employee ID.
Line 2: monthly salary.
extra_fields.output_format:
ID: <id>
Salary: <salary to 2 decimal places>

questions.title: Temperature Conversion Object
questions.objective: Store a value in an object through its constructor and compute a derived value with a method.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Temperature with a private double field celsius. Its constructor must initialize this field. Implement toFahrenheit(), which returns the converted temperature using:

Fahrenheit = Celsius × 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0

Read the Celsius value, construct the object, call the method, and print both temperatures to exactly two decimal places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: 25°C converts to 77°F.
questions.input_format: One line containing the Celsius temperature.
questions.output_format:
Celsius: <value to 2 decimal places>
Fahrenheit: <value to 2 decimal places>
hints: Use 9.0 / 5.0, not 9 / 5: integer division would give 1.
Add a getter for celsius, because the field is private.
Format both values with String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f", value).

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing the Celsius temperature.
extra_fields.output_format:
Celsius: <value to 2 decimal places>
Fahrenheit: <value to 2 decimal places>

questions.title: Method Overloading in a Calculator
questions.objective: Declare overloaded instance methods that differ by parameter count and type.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Calculator with these overloaded methods:
- add(int a, int b) returns the sum of two integers.
- add(int a, int b, int c) returns the sum of three integers.
- add(double a, double b) returns the sum of two decimal numbers.
Read the seven input values in the specified order. Call the matching overload for each group and print each result on a separate line. Format the decimal result to two places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Java selects the correct overload based on the number and types of arguments.
questions.input_format:
Lines 1–2: two integers.
Lines 3–5: three integers.
Lines 6–7: two decimal numbers.
questions.output_format: Print the first sum, second sum, and decimal sum on separate lines.
hints: All three methods are named add; Java tells them apart by their parameter lists.
Read the last two values as doubles so the add(double, double) version is chosen.
Only the decimal result is formatted with two places.

extra_fields.input_format:
Lines 1–2: two integers.
Lines 3–5: three integers.
Lines 6–7: two decimal numbers.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the first sum, second sum, and decimal sum on separate lines.

questions.title: Product Inventory with Validation
questions.objective: Encapsulate state and allow changes only through a method that validates each request.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Product with private fields name (String), price (long), and quantity (int). Initialize all fields through a constructor and provide public getters.

Implement sell(int count). It must reduce quantity only when count is positive and no greater than the available quantity. Invalid requests must leave quantity unchanged.

Read the product details and sale requests, process the requests in order, and print the final product details.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The sale of 20 is rejected because only 8 remain after the first sale. The final sale leaves 5 units.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: product name, without spaces.
Line 2: price.
Line 3: initial quantity.
Line 4: number of sale requests, N.
Next N lines: requested quantities.
questions.output_format:
Product: <name>
Price: <price>
Quantity: <remaining quantity>
questions.constraints:
Name length: 1–50
0 ≤ price ≤ 10^12
0 ≤ initial quantity ≤ 1,000,000
0 ≤ N ≤ 100
1 ≤ each sale request ≤ 1,000,000
hints: Store price as a long, because it can reach 10^12.
In sell, check count > 0 && count <= quantity before subtracting.
A sale equal to the remaining quantity is valid and leaves 0.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: product name, without spaces.
Line 2: price.
Line 3: initial quantity.
Line 4: number of sale requests, N.
Next N lines: requested quantities.
extra_fields.output_format:
Product: <name>
Price: <price>
Quantity: <remaining quantity>

questions.title: Count Objects Using a Static Field
questions.objective: Use a static field shared by all instances to count constructed objects.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Ticket with a private instance field ticketId and a private static field createdCount, initially zero. Every time a Ticket object is constructed, increment createdCount by one.

Implement a constructor to initialize ticketId and a public static method getCreatedCount() that returns the total number of constructed objects.

Read N ticket IDs, construct one object for each ID, and print the count. Duplicate IDs still represent separate objects.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Four objects were constructed, so the static count is 4.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: ticket IDs.
questions.output_format: Print the number of constructed objects.
hints: A static field belongs to the class, so every Ticket object shares one createdCount.
Increase createdCount inside the constructor.
Call the static method on the class: Ticket.getCreatedCount().

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: ticket IDs.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the number of constructed objects.

questions.title: Inheritance: Vehicle Toll Calculation
questions.objective: Override a base-class method in subclasses and call it through a base-class reference.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a base class Vehicle with a protected field vehicleNumber (String) and a constructor that initializes it. Implement a public method calculateToll() that returns a default toll of 50.

Create two subclasses:
- Car overrides calculateToll() to return 100.
- Truck overrides calculateToll() to return 200.
Read the vehicle type and number, create the corresponding object, and call calculateToll() through a Vehicle reference. Print the vehicle number and toll. This must demonstrate method overriding through inheritance.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The object is a Truck, so its overridden method returns 200 rather than the base class's default toll.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: C for car or T for truck.
Line 2: vehicle number, without spaces.
questions.output_format:
Vehicle: <vehicle number>
Toll: <calculated toll>
questions.constraints:
Vehicle number length: 1–20
Type is always C or T.
hints: Each subclass constructor passes the number to the parent with super(vehicleNumber).
Declare the variable as Vehicle v and assign either new Car(...) or new Truck(...).
v.calculateToll() runs the subclass's version, chosen at runtime.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: C for car or T for truck.
Line 2: vehicle number, without spaces.
extra_fields.output_format:
Vehicle: <vehicle number>
Toll: <calculated toll>

questions.title: Method Overriding: Shape Area
questions.objective: Override a method in two subclasses with different fields and formulas.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Shape with a public method area() that returns 0.0. Create two subclasses:
- Circle stores a radius and overrides area() to return π × radius × radius.
- Rectangle stores length and width and overrides area() to return length × width.
Read the shape type and its dimensions, create the matching object, and invoke area() through a Shape reference. Use π = 3.141592653589793. Print the result to two decimal places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The circle's area is π × 2 × 2, which rounds to 12.57.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: C or R.
For C, line 2 is the radius.
For R, line 2 is length and line 3 is width.
questions.output_format: Area: <area to 2 decimal places>
questions.constraints: 0.01 ≤ each dimension ≤ 100,000
hints: Read the dimensions inside the branch for the chosen type, because circles have one dimension and rectangles have two.
Store the object in a Shape variable and call area() on it.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: C or R.
For C, line 2 is the radius.
For R, line 2 is length and line 3 is width.
extra_fields.output_format: Area: <area to 2 decimal places>

questions.title: toString() for a Book Object
questions.objective: Override toString() so that printing an object produces a custom description.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Book with private fields title (String), author (String), and year (int). Implement a constructor that initializes all fields. Override toString() to return exactly this format:

Book{title='<title>', author='<author>', year=<year>}

In main(), read the three values, create a Book object, and print the object directly using System.out.println(book). Do not manually reproduce the output string in main().

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Printing the object invokes its overridden toString() method.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: title, without spaces.
Line 2: author, without spaces.
Line 3: publication year.
questions.output_format: Print the exact string returned by toString().
questions.constraints:
Title and author lengths: 1–50
0 ≤ year ≤ 3000
hints: Declare it as @Override public String toString().
Build the string with concatenation, including the single quotes around title and author.
System.out.println(book) calls toString() automatically.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: title, without spaces.
Line 2: author, without spaces.
Line 3: publication year.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the exact string returned by toString().

questions.title: equals() for Comparing Points
questions.objective: Override equals() to compare objects by their field values instead of their references.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Point with private integer fields x and y. Implement a constructor that initializes both fields and override equals(Object obj) so that two Point objects are equal when their x-coordinates and y-coordinates are both equal.

Your implementation must return false when the argument is null or is not a Point. It must compare coordinate values, not object references.

In main(), read two points, create two separate objects, and print EQUAL if the first object's equals() method returns true for the second; otherwise, print NOT EQUAL.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The two objects are separate instances, but both store the coordinates (3, 5). Therefore, they are equal according to the overridden method.
questions.input_format:
Lines 1–2: coordinates x1 and y1.
Lines 3–4: coordinates x2 and y2.
questions.output_format: Print EQUAL or NOT EQUAL.
questions.constraints: −1,000,000 ≤ each coordinate ≤ 1,000,000
hints: The parameter type must be Object, not Point, or you overload equals instead of overriding it.
Return false if obj is not an instance of Point, using instanceof; this also handles null.
Cast obj to Point and compare both x and y.

extra_fields.input_format:
Lines 1–2: coordinates x1 and y1.
Lines 3–4: coordinates x2 and y2.
extra_fields.output_format: Print EQUAL or NOT EQUAL.

questions.title: Constructor Chaining with this()
questions.objective: Call one constructor from another with this() to avoid repeating initialization code.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Box with private integer fields length, width, and height.

Implement two constructors:
- Box(int side): creates a cube by setting all three dimensions to side.
- Box(int length, int width, int height): initializes each dimension independently.
The one-argument constructor must call the three-argument constructor using this(). Implement volume() returning length × width × height as a long. Convert to long before multiplying, because the volume can reach 10^12, which exceeds the int range.

Read a mode. If the mode is C, read one side length and create a cube. If the mode is R, read three dimensions and create a rectangular box. Print the volume.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The one-argument constructor calls the three-argument constructor with dimensions 4, 4, and 4. The volume is 64.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: C or R.
For C: line 2 contains side length.
For R: lines 2–4 contain length, width, and height.
questions.output_format: Print Volume: followed by a space and the volume as an integer.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ each dimension ≤ 10,000
The volume fits in a Java long.
hints: Inside Box(int side), the first statement is this(side, side, side);.
this(...) must be the first statement in the constructor.
Return (long) length * width * height; casting first makes the whole multiplication use long.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: C or R.
For C: line 2 contains side length.
For R: lines 2–4 contain length, width, and height.
extra_fields.output_format: Print Volume: followed by a space and the volume as an integer.

questions.title: Interface: Payment Processing
questions.objective: Implement an interface in two classes and call the method through an interface reference.
questions.problem_statement:
Create an interface PaymentMethod declaring pay(long amount), which returns the final charge.

Implement two classes:
- CardPayment: charges a fee of 2% of the amount.
- UPIPayment: charges no fee.
For card payments, calculate the fee as amount × 2 / 100 using integer arithmetic, truncating any fractional part. The final charge is the amount plus the fee.

Read the payment type and amount, create the appropriate object, and call pay() through a PaymentMethod reference. Print the final charge.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The card fee is 20, so the final charge is 1020.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: CARD or UPI.
Line 2: amount.
questions.output_format: Print Final Charge: followed by a space and the final charge.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ amount ≤ 10^12
The final charge fits in a Java long.
hints: Classes use implements PaymentMethod and must provide a public pay method.
Compare the type with .equals("CARD"), not ==.
Integer division truncates the fee, so an amount of 49 has a fee of 0.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: CARD or UPI.
Line 2: amount.
extra_fields.output_format: Print Final Charge: followed by a space and the final charge.

questions.title: Calling super.method() in an Override
questions.objective: Extend inherited behavior by calling super.method() inside an overriding method.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a base class Notification with a method message() returning the string Notification received.

Create a subclass UrgentNotification that overrides message(). Its implementation must call super.message() and append the text " - URGENT" (beginning with a space) to the returned string, producing Notification received - URGENT.

Read a notification type, create either a Notification object for type N or an UrgentNotification object for type U, and call message() through a Notification reference. Print the returned string.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The subclass uses super.message() to reuse the base implementation and adds its urgent suffix.
questions.input_format: One line containing N or U.
questions.output_format: Print the exact string returned by the selected object's message() method.
questions.constraints: The type is always N or U.
hints: In the subclass, return super.message() + " - URGENT";.
Do not copy the base text into the subclass; calling super keeps both in sync.
Store the object in a Notification variable for both types.

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing N or U.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the exact string returned by the selected object's message() method.

questions.title: Abstract Class: Subscription Billing
questions.objective: Implement an abstract method in two subclasses and process an array of mixed objects polymorphically.
questions.problem_statement:
Create an abstract class Subscription with private fields customerId (int) and monthlyFee (long). Its constructor initializes both fields, and it provides public getter methods. Declare an abstract method calculateBill(int months) returning a long.

Create two subclasses:
- StandardSubscription: the bill is the monthly fee multiplied by the number of months.
- PremiumSubscription: the bill is the monthly fee multiplied by the number of months, plus a one-time activation fee of 500 if the subscription period is greater than zero. If the number of months is zero, the bill is zero.
Read N subscription records, create the corresponding subclass for each record, and store the objects in a Subscription array. Calculate and print each bill in input order, followed by the total bill. Invoke calculateBill() through a Subscription reference.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The standard subscription costs 3 × 1000 = 3000. The premium subscription costs 2 × 2000 + 500 = 4500. The third subscription has zero months, so its bill is zero.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each subscription:
- Line 1: S for standard or P for premium.
- Line 2: customer ID.
- Line 3: monthly fee.
- Line 4: number of months.
questions.output_format:
For each subscription, print:
Customer <id>: <bill>
After all records, print:
Total Bill: <total>
If N = 0, print Total Bill: 0.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 1000
1 ≤ customer ID ≤ 1,000,000
0 ≤ monthly fee ≤ 10^9
0 ≤ months ≤ 120
All bills and the total fit in a Java long.
hints: Subclasses read the private monthlyFee through getMonthlyFee().
Store the months for each record alongside the object, for example in an int array of the same length.
In PremiumSubscription, return 0 when months is 0; otherwise add the 500 activation fee.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each subscription:
- Line 1: S for standard or P for premium.
- Line 2: customer ID.
- Line 3: monthly fee.
- Line 4: number of months.
extra_fields.output_format:
For each subscription, print:
Customer <id>: <bill>
After all records, print:
Total Bill: <total>
If N = 0, print Total Bill: 0.

questions.title: Multiple Interfaces: Smart Device
questions.objective: Implement two interfaces in one class and use the same object through either interface type.
questions.problem_statement:
Create two interfaces:
- Connectable, declaring connect(), which returns a string describing the connection status.
- Controllable, declaring performAction(String action), which returns a string describing the performed action.
Create a class SmartSpeaker that implements both interfaces.

Its connect() method must return SmartSpeaker connected.

Its performAction(action) method must return Action performed: followed by a space and the supplied action, preserving the action's characters exactly.

In main(), create one SmartSpeaker object. Store it in a Connectable reference and call connect(). Then store the same object in a Controllable reference and call performAction().

Input implementation hint: Read the action as a complete line. Avoid reading it with next() because that would discard everything after the first space.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The same object can be accessed through either interface reference because SmartSpeaker implements both interfaces.
questions.input_format: One line containing the action. The line may contain spaces.
questions.output_format: Print the connection result on the first line and the action result on the second line.
questions.constraints:
Action length: 1–200 characters.
All characters are printable ASCII.
sample_outputs:
SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Play classical music

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Volume up
hints: Declare the class as class SmartSpeaker implements Connectable, Controllable.
Create one object, then assign it to both a Connectable variable and a Controllable variable.
Read the action with sc.nextLine() so spaces are kept.

test_cases.output:
SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Play classical music

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Volume up

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Set alarm for 7:00 AM!

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Turn off

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed:   leading spaces

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: A b C d

SmartSpeaker connected
Action performed: Call Mom @ 5:30pm

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing the action. The line may contain spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the connection result on the first line and the action result on the second line.

questions.title: Composition: Shopping Cart Total
questions.objective: Build a class that contains and operates on an array of objects of another class.
questions.problem_statement:
Implement a shopping cart using composition.

Create a class CartItem with private fields productName (String), unitPrice (long), and quantity (int). Its constructor initializes all fields. Implement subtotal() to return unit price multiplied by quantity.

Create a class ShoppingCart that contains an array of CartItem objects. Its constructor receives the capacity of the array. Implement addItem(CartItem item) to add an item to the next available position and calculateTotal() to return the sum of all item subtotals.

In main(), read N items, create a ShoppingCart with capacity N, create one CartItem per input record, add each item to the cart, and print every item's subtotal followed by the cart total. This problem must use object composition: ShoppingCart contains and operates on CartItem objects.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The subtotals are 1000, 1500, and 600. Their sum is 3100.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each item:
- Line 1: product name, without spaces.
- Line 2: unit price.
- Line 3: quantity.
questions.output_format:
For each item, print:
<product name>: <subtotal>
After all items, print:
Cart Total: <total>
If N = 0, print Cart Total: 0.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 1000
Product name length: 1–50 characters.
0 ≤ unit price ≤ 10^9
0 ≤ quantity ≤ 1,000,000
The cart total fits in a Java long.
hints: ShoppingCart keeps a CartItem[] items array and an int count of items added so far.
addItem stores the item at items[count] and then increases count.
subtotal() multiplies a long by an int, so the result is a long; calculateTotal() adds the first count subtotals.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each item:
- Line 1: product name, without spaces.
- Line 2: unit price.
- Line 3: quantity.
extra_fields.output_format:
For each item, print:
<product name>: <subtotal>
After all items, print:
Cart Total: <total>
If N = 0, print Cart Total: 0.

questions.title: Polymorphic Shipping Cost Calculator
questions.objective: Use an abstract class with three subclasses to compute costs for a mixed array of objects.
questions.problem_statement:
Create an abstract class ShippingService with a protected field weight (double), initialized by its constructor. Declare an abstract method calculateCost() that returns a double.

Implement three subclasses:
- StandardShipping: cost is 50 + 10 × weight.
- ExpressShipping: cost is 100 + 20 × weight.
- InternationalShipping: cost is 200 + 30 × weight.
Read N shipping requests, create the appropriate subclass for each request, and store the objects in a ShippingService array. Call calculateCost() through a ShippingService reference for each object. Print each cost in input order and then the total cost, formatting all monetary values to exactly two decimal places using Locale.US.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The three formulas produce 70, 140, and 260. Their total is 470.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each request:
- Line 1: S for standard, E for express, or I for international.
- Line 2: package weight in kilograms.
questions.output_format:
For each request, print:
Shipping Cost: <cost to 2 decimal places>
After all requests, print:
Total Shipping Cost: <total to 2 decimal places>
If N = 0, print Total Shipping Cost: 0.00.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 1000
0.01 ≤ weight ≤ 1000, with at most two decimal places
Type is always S, E, or I.
All calculated values fit in a double.

questions.title: Equality and Hashing for Unique Products
questions.objective: Override equals() and hashCode() consistently and use equals() to count distinct objects.
questions.problem_statement:
Create a class Product with private fields productId (int) and name (String). Its constructor initializes both fields.

Override equals(Object obj) so that two Product objects are considered equal if and only if their productId values match. The product names do not affect equality.

Also override hashCode() so that equal products have equal hash codes. You may use the product ID's integer value as the hash code.

In main(), read N product records, create one Product object per record, and count how many distinct product IDs occur. Do not use collections: compare each new product with the products already encountered using equals().

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare the other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The IDs are 101, 102, 101, 103, and 102. Only three distinct IDs exist. Different names do not make products with the same ID unequal.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
For each product:
- Line 1: product ID.
- Line 2: product name, without spaces.
questions.output_format: Print the number of distinct products according to the specified equality rule.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 1000
1 ≤ product ID ≤ 1,000,000
Product name length: 1–50 characters.
hints: equals must take an Object parameter and use instanceof before casting.
hashCode can simply return productId, so equal products always have equal hash codes.
Store the products in an array; a product is new if equals() is false for every earlier product.
